newsitem.title: UK: Give every British child E-mail address - report.
newsitem.headline: Give every British child E-mail address - report.

text.p: Britain's opposition Party leader Tony Blair on Thursday welcomed an independent report calling for every British child to have access to a computer and to have his or her own E-mail address.
But Blair said he could not commit the Labour government he hopes to form after the May 1 election to providing extra resources to allow this to happen.
The report was commissioned by Labour from a committee under the chairmanship of Dennis Stevenson, chairman of GPA Group Plc and chairman elect of Pearson Plc.

"I like the idea that every child over the age of nine and every adult should have their own E-mail address, accessible from school, home, library or cybercafe, symbolising the personal stake they will have in the new education technology of the future," Blair told a news conference.
"The Committee say it is a low-cost initiative. We will be examining just how low-cost, and how soon it can be done."

But in answer to questions, Blair stressed that although the priority of his government would be to improve education, it would not be willing to compromise on its commitment to keep government spending totals down in order to do so.

However, Blair announced that Stevenson had agreed to chair a Standing Committee under a Labour government "to help drive forward the implementation of our plans on the use of new technology in schools."

The Stevenson report says children who do not have access to a computer at home should be given access to one via a programme which would be analogous to the building up of public libraries in the 19th century.

It calls for teachers to receive tax breaks when they buy their own computers for school or home use and says a minister in the Department of Education should be given a specific remit to improve information technology in schools. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
